input.quote: 3.19 Exclusivity Commitment of SFJ. During the applicable Exclusive Period, SFJ shall not, and shall cause its Affiliates not to, either by itself or through a Third Party, conduct human clinical trials of, or sell, offer for sale or have sold:
input.rationale: The Agreement imposes no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on us, so it meets the preferred position. The only exclusivity covenant (§ 3.19, p0369–p0374) runs against SFJ during the Exclusive Period and therefore benefits us — under the rule this is expressly acceptable and not flagged. The § 2.4 Approved CRO / Approved Vendor architecture (p0262–p0264) applies reciprocally to each Party and lets us contract with any listed or JDC-approved provider; it is a joint-governance quality gate, not a requirements or single-source commitment, and does not channel our sourcing to SFJ. § 3.14.2.1 (p0359) restricts SFJ to using Product supplied by us, and § 3.14.1.1 (p0355) confirms we manufacture directly or through an Approved Vendor of our choosing — again in our favour. Restrictions in § 7.5 (e.g. the Licensing Transaction consent at p0552) limit out-licensing and financing rather than our freedom to buy from other suppliers, and are addressed under the financing/restrictive-covenant rules rather than this one. No redline required.
